children: Hungary's central bank needs to maintain a sufficient buffer on real interest rates amid volatility in global markets driven by conflicts such as the Iran war, central bank Governor Mihaly Varga told an economics conference on Thursday.
He added however that Hungary's real interest rate level could fall if the country makes progress in its euro adoption efforts. The central bank's next policy meeting is due on September 22.
